title: A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions

concept.text: Conceptual synthesis: A general functional decoder would infer what an unfamiliar gene product does from its sequence and available biological context, including cases without close, experimentally characterized relatives. Its outputs would be specific, testable hypotheses: an enzyme’s substrates and products, a protein’s binding partners, or the conditions under which a molecular activity contributes to a cellular process. Assigning a broad category would be useful intermediate information, but would not by itself fulfill this concept.

Scope synthesis: The proposed capability connects sequence interpretation with biochemistry, functional genomics and systems biology. It would distinguish a molecule’s activity from its role in an organism: identifying a reaction or binding interaction does not automatically establish when that activity occurs or what biological consequence it produces. A useful decoder would therefore express both the predicted function and the contextual limits and uncertainty of that prediction. This is a hypothetical capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: Reliable, detailed interpretation of deeply unfamiliar gene products would turn more of the biological sequence record into experimentally actionable knowledge. The direct advance would be the ability to predict and then confirm previously unknown molecular activities, including potentially those encoded by uncultivated organisms. This could reveal unfamiliar chemistry and biological systems while helping researchers choose informative experiments.

Conditional downstream synthesis: Confirmed activities could provide starting points for medicines, industrial enzymes or engineered pathways. Those outcomes would still require additional work on mechanism, performance, delivery, safety or integration into a useful system. The decoder analogy also has limits: sequence would not necessarily specify one fixed, context-independent function, and a correct molecular prediction would not alone explain an organism’s behavior. The revolutionary prospect is broader access to specific functional knowledge, with experimental confirmation and contextual interpretation remaining essential.

missing_breakthrough.text: Capability-gap synthesis: The missing capability is reliable inference of detailed activity and biological context when similarity to characterized examples provides little guidance. The proposed decoder would need to move beyond recognizable families and broad labels to distinguish particular substrates, products or partners, including unfamiliar chemistry. The supplied review regards this as a coherent scientific goal, but the available source material does not independently document how broadly present methods fall short or establish the current boundary of the field.

Engineering-barrier synthesis: A convincing system would need to separate evidence for a specific molecular activity from evidence that a gene merely participates in the same process as other genes. It would also need to distinguish biochemical capability from activity under particular cellular conditions, and represent uncertainty when several functions remain plausible. Evaluation must make distance from characterized examples explicit so that performance on familiar relatives does not stand in for performance on unfamiliar families.

Validation-barrier synthesis: Detailed predictions require experiments suited to the proposed chemistry or interaction. Cellular experiments would then test whether that activity has the predicted contextual role. Negative results are especially difficult to interpret: failure to detect activity can reflect the conditions or sensitivity of an assay. Establishing a bounded absence under specified conditions is different from establishing that a gene product has no function.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes to FUGAsseM predictions for more than 443,000 microbial protein families, including families with weak or no homology to known proteins, using community multiomics data. It identifies the associated work as Zhang et al., “Predicting functions of uncharacterized gene products from microbial communities,” dated October 15, 2025, with DOI 10.1038/s41587-025-02813-7. These are retained as attributed claims: the supplied review could not verify the article’s identity, date, family count, homology scope or method from the available artifact.

According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie challenge, with no inspectable abstract or scientific results. Consequently, the earlier description of the evidence as abstract-level access is not justified. The research also reports earlier publisher and archive fetch failures, but those events are not documented by the retained material. The access limitation leaves the scientific claims unverified here; it does not establish that they are false.

Interpretive synthesis: Even if the attributed FUGAsseM account is accurate, its reported scale concerns putative functional annotations, not experimental determination of every family’s chemistry or cellular role. Such predictions would represent progress toward this concept, while leaving their specificity, accuracy and experimental coverage to be established. The supplied material establishes neither a completed general decoder nor a comprehensive account of demonstrated progress. Its empty freshness record also prevents assessment of field coverage as of November 1, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Before experiments begin, a system would predict detailed functions for a diverse, blinded sample of poorly characterized gene families, including families without close annotated relatives. The evaluation would define family diversity, distance from characterized examples, confidence thresholds and success criteria in advance. Predictions would specify substrates, products, binding partners or similarly discriminating functional details; broad labels alone would not satisfy the proposal.
completion_criteria.label: Detailed blinded predictions cover families without close annotated relatives

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: Independent biochemical experiments would test the predicted activities, and cellular experiments would test relevant biological roles. Testing would include positive predictions and confidently predicted absences, with assay conditions, detection limits and the scope of each negative conclusion stated explicitly. Results would distinguish an incorrect activity prediction from an activity that remains undetected under the tested conditions, without treating either explanation as automatically established.
completion_criteria.label: Independent biochemical and cellular tests assess predicted functions and absences

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Convincing evidence would include independently reproducible results across the defined range of families, transparent reporting of failures and uncertainty, and sufficient experimental detail to repeat the tests. Performance would be reported separately for different levels of annotation distance and functional specificity. These are proposed criteria, not established community standards. A finite evaluation could demonstrate substantial breadth within its tested domain, but could not establish literal universality across all genes, organisms and environments.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproducibility across families with stratified performance and uncertainty reporting

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-12, “Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities,” has the closest supplied overlap: community data can support functional inference, while functional predictions can enrich community profiles. BIF-12 centers on resolving and interpreting mixed microbial communities; BIF-06 centers on understanding unfamiliar gene products more generally, whether or not they occur in a community dataset. BIF-11, “Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes,” could supply reconstructed sequences, but sequence assembly and functional interpretation are distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-02, “Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence,” and BIF-09, “Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities,” concern physical behavior and interactions that could inform functional interpretation. Binding partners are one possible output shared with BIF-06, but predicting an interaction or molecular motion does not by itself establish a gene product’s full activity or cellular role. BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” addresses how genomic regulation controls biological activity, whereas BIF-06 focuses on the activities of gene products.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” and BIF-08, “Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates,” place molecular functions within broader biological systems. Functional annotations could inform these models, while systems context could help discriminate among functional hypotheses. Their respective targets—cell behavior, causal networks, molecular organization and cell fate—remain distinct from decoding an unfamiliar gene product.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” could use reliable functional predictions when selecting and combining biological components. Understanding a component does not establish that a designed genome, circuit or pathway will work. BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” could incorporate functional decoding within a larger discovery workflow; BIF-06 remains a specific scientific capability rather than the entire autonomous workflow.

change_log.reason: The research supplies the core goal, while the review clarifies why broad labels and context-free interpretations would be insufficient.

change_log.change: Preserved the distinction between putative annotation and experimental elucidation, and separated direct scientific advances from conditional applications.
change_log.reason: Large-scale predictions do not establish detailed chemistry for every family, and confirmed activities do not by themselves deliver medicines or industrial systems.

change_log.change: Made the proposed evaluation operational through predefined diversity, annotation distance, confidence, success criteria, independent experiments and bounded negative claims.
change_log.reason: These additions preserve the original prospective demonstration while making its breadth and interpretation assessable.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not verify the FUGAsseM article’s identity, publication date, DOI, family count, homology scope, methods, predictive accuracy or experimental validation coverage.
The earlier publisher and archive fetch failures cannot be reconstructed from the retained artifact; an abstract-level evidence description remains unjustified.

The supplied evidence does not independently establish the present boundary of detailed functional prediction for unfamiliar gene families, and the empty freshness record prevents assessment of coverage as of November 1, 2026.

The proposed demonstration still requires concrete choices of family sampling, annotation-distance measures, confidence thresholds, success criteria, assay conditions and detection limits. No numerical thresholds are established by these inputs.

brief.title: Finding out what unfamiliar genes do
possible: Researchers could take an unfamiliar gene and predict what its protein does, even without a well-understood relative for comparison. They could identify the chemicals it changes, the molecules it binds, and the conditions in which it helps a cell.
why: More of the growing collection of biological sequences would become useful knowledge. Researchers could choose experiments that uncover unfamiliar chemistry and biological systems, including those in organisms they cannot grow in the laboratory.
Confirmed functions could give researchers starting points for medicines, industrial enzymes—proteins that speed up chemical reactions—and engineered chains of reactions.

sources.showed: Their tool, FUGAsseM, predicted functions for more than 443,000 microbial protein families using measurements across microbial communities. These included families without recognizable sequence similarity to known proteins.
sources.quote: We predict high-confidence functions for >443,000 protein families
sources.cited_for: Community measurements can help predict functions beyond familiar protein families.
sources.not_established: Predicted functions do not establish each family's detailed chemistry or role inside cells.

sources.showed: Their tool, EZSpecificity, predicted which chemicals enzymes could act on. Laboratory tests supported its predictions in a selected group of enzymes.
sources.quote:
EZSpecificity outperformed the 
existing machine learning models for enzyme substrate specificity prediction, as 
demonstrated by both an unknown substrate and enzyme database and seven 
proof-of-concept protein families.
sources.cited_for: Predictions can distinguish the chemicals an enzyme acts on, beyond assigning a broad function.
sources.not_established: Selected enzyme tests do not establish detailed functions across unfamiliar protein families or their roles in cells.

sources.showed: Their tool, CATNIP, ranked compatible enzymes and chemicals within a particular enzyme group. Laboratory tests confirmed predicted activity for a previously uncharacterized enzyme with a characterized relative.
sources.quote: We examined diverse substrates and protein sequences for new biocatalytic reactions and use these data to build machine learning models to predict compatible enzymes and substrates.
sources.cited_for: Predictions can guide experiments that identify previously unknown enzyme activity.
sources.not_established: Success within a particular enzyme group does not establish prediction for proteins without characterized relatives.

sources.showed: This preprint found that existing tools struggled on unfamiliar enzyme and chemical combinations. An approach using predicted molecular interactions consistently beat sequence comparisons on their enzyme-ranking test.
sources.quote:
We again find that most
models do not outperform sequence-based (BLAST) baselines even after fine-tuning.
sources.cited_for: Tests using unfamiliar examples can expose weaknesses hidden by other measures of prediction accuracy.
sources.not_established: The improved ranking result does not establish general function prediction, and the work remains a preprint.

sources.who: M Clara De Paolis Kaluza and colleagues
sources.showed: This preprint reported improved protein function predictions in a community competition. Predictions were assessed against experimental findings that became available after submission.
sources.quote: In this work, we present an in-depth analysis of the submitted predictions and report improvements in accuracy over all methods from the previous CAFA challenges.
sources.cited_for: Independent assessment against later experimental findings shows progress in protein function prediction.
sources.not_established: Improved function labels do not establish detailed chemistry and cellular roles across deeply unfamiliar families.

shown: Zhang and colleagues have predicted functions across a large range of microbial protein families. Cui's and Paton's teams have gone further on selected enzymes, using laboratory experiments to test which chemicals they act on.

The reach of these successes remains limited. Mahood and colleagues' preprint found that existing tools struggled when both enzymes and chemicals were unfamiliar. No general system has demonstrated detailed molecular functions together with their roles inside cells.
missing: Reliable, detailed predictions for diverse protein families without close, experimentally characterized relatives remain to be demonstrated.
Experiments must establish both a protein's molecular activity and when that activity contributes to a cellular process.
Independent teams must reproduce results across unfamiliar families, with failures and uncertainty reported.

milestones.label: Detailed predictions succeed for families without close characterized relatives
milestones.explanation: A system would have to make detailed predictions on a diverse, blinded sample before experiments, under predefined criteria. This would test whether it can move beyond familiar relatives and broad labels.

milestones.label: Independent experiments test activities, cellular roles and predicted absences
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratory and cellular tests would have to assess predicted functions and absences under stated conditions and detection limits. This would distinguish wrong predictions from activity the tests could not detect.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results across families with clear limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results across the defined families, reporting failures, uncertainty and accuracy by distance from known examples and level of detail. This would establish the system's practical reach.

uncertain: The required family diversity, distance from characterized examples and success thresholds remain to be defined.
A failed experiment may reflect unsuitable conditions or limited sensitivity rather than an absent function.
A finite evaluation can establish breadth within its tested range, but cannot establish success across all genes, organisms and environments.

page.title: Function prediction for uncharacterized protein families
page.definition: A computational method infers a protein's specific molecular activity and its role under stated cellular conditions from sequence and biological context, including families without close experimentally characterized relatives. Predictions identify reaction substrates and products, binding partners or equivalent molecular details.

goal.need: On 25 March 2022, UniProt's approximately 21,000 reference organisms encoded over 64 million proteins, but about 72,000, or 0.1%, were directly linked to experimental evidence of function. Computational inference addresses this disparity between sequence availability and experimentally established function.

figures.caption: Functional evidence in UniProt reference organisms on 25 March 2022
rows: Directly linked to experimental functional evidence
figures.note: This historical snapshot covers reference organisms. Experimental evidence does not imply that every activity or cellular role is known.

completion.title: Independent laboratories confirm molecular and cellular predictions across uncharacterized protein families.
completion.criterion: Independent laboratories prospectively confirm one frozen method's predictions of specific molecular activities and conditional cellular roles for a predeclared set of proteins from previously uncharacterized families lacking close experimentally characterized relatives. Biochemical assays establish the predicted reactions or interactions; cellular perturbations establish the predicted roles under stated conditions. Replication uses a separate target set. Achievement is limited to the tested domain; no universal accuracy or family-coverage threshold is asserted.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis; no outside body located publishes a completion test for this combined capability.
completion.basis: Searched NIST's Protein Function Problem programme, DARPA DUF and NODES documents, CAFA protocols, the 2022 community roadmap and IUBMB criteria. None defines a joint pass threshold for specific molecular activity, conditional cellular role and generalization across uncharacterized families. This bounded test combines their stated goals and experimental requirements; it does not certify universal decoding.

milestones.title: A protein catalyses its predicted substrate-to-product reaction in direct experiments.
milestones.criterion: Direct experiments establish the predicted enzyme-catalysed substrate-to-product reaction. CATNIP, published on 1 October 2025, tested TqaL's 12 top-ranked substrates in triplicate: four were oxidized, including the second-ranked substrate at 42% conversion; TqaL has a characterized homologue. EZSpecificity, published on 8 October 2025, tested eight halogenases and 78 substrates and reported 91.7% top-choice accuracy on 12 new substrates after family-specific fine-tuning.
milestones.set_by: Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Enzyme Nomenclature, Criteria for inclusion; published for enzyme reactions.
milestones.threshold_quote: Before an enzyme can be included in the list direct experimental evidence is required that the proposed enzyme actually catalyses the reaction claimed.

milestones.title: Prospective protein function predictions outperform CAFA's sequence and frequency baselines.
milestones.criterion: Predictions precede the experimental annotations used for evaluation. A method exceeds CAFA's BLAST sequence-transfer and Naive frequency baselines in information-weighted maximum F1, separately for molecular function, biological process and cellular component. CAFA5 evaluated 1,717 proteins without prior experimental Gene Ontology annotations and reports top methods above baselines (preprint, 10 June 2026; not peer reviewed). Separately, FUGAsseM inferred functions for >443,000 families from 1,595 gut metagenomes and 800 metatranscriptomes; these counts measure putative annotation coverage.
milestones.set_by: CAFA organizers, CAFA5 prospective No-Knowledge protocol and published baseline comparisons. No-Knowledge describes annotation status; homologue distance is unrestricted.
milestones.threshold_quote: In all cases, the top-ten methods outperformed all baseline methods.

milestones.title: Enzyme ranking beats BLAST below 40% sequence identity and 0.7 substrate similarity to training data.
milestones.criterion: Exceed both BLAST baselines for correct-enzyme retrieval in the top 10%, 20% and 50% of candidate lists in Mahood et al.'s P450 benchmark. Its 45 held-out reactions have enzyme sequence identity <40% and substrate Tanimoto fingerprint similarity <0.7 to the remaining dataset; each source organism supplies at least ten candidate P450s. The preprint, submitted on 6 July 2026 and not peer reviewed, reports consistent improvement for classifiers using Boltz interaction representations. The source dataset contains 2,922 reactions across 768 enzymes.
milestones.set_by: Mahood and colleagues, published cytochrome P450 ranking protocol and BLAST comparisons; the novelty thresholds were specified for this enzyme-class benchmark.
milestones.threshold_quote: the correct enzyme within the top 10, 20 or 50% of enzymes.

milestones.title: A predicted Candida biofilm gene yields smooth or intermediate colonies after two days at 37°C.
milestones.criterion: A predicted Candida albicans biofilm gene meets CAFA-π's positive definition: deletion or repression produces smooth or intermediate colonies on Spider agar at 37°C after two days, versus wrinkled wild type. GRACE strains use 100 μg/ml doxycycline. Screening covered 2,746 genes and found 245 colony-biofilm positives. No tested predictor exceeded AUROC 0.60 for biofilm formation in either screened microbe. This establishes a condition-specific phenotype; molecular activity requires a separate test.
milestones.set_by: CAFA organizers, Candida albicans experimental protocol published on 19 November 2019; this phenotype criterion was specified for Candida biofilm formation.
milestones.threshold_quote: A protein is considered true in the biofilm function, if its mutant phenotype is smooth or intermediate under doxycycline.

milestones.title: Experiments confirm one method's molecular and cellular predictions across uncharacterized families.
milestones.criterion: One computational method makes prospective predictions of both specific molecular activity and conditional cellular role for proteins from multiple uncharacterized families lacking close characterized relatives. Biochemical assays confirm the predicted reactions or interactions, and cellular perturbations confirm the predicted roles under the stated conditions. This joint demonstration precedes independent testing on a separate target set. The cited programmes publish no joint numerical accuracy, family-count or homology-distance threshold.
milestones.set_by: Atlas synthesis; searches of NIST, DARPA DUF/NODES and CAFA documents found no published test for this joint demonstration.

not_found: No field-wide numerical definition of a close characterized relative was found for the combined molecular-and-cellular prediction task.

results.detail: The evaluation used annotations added after the training-data cutoff, but the paper does not report the required information-weighted maximum F1 comparison against both CAFA baselines for each GO aspect. Its coverage of 443,549 families measures putative annotations.

results.finding: EZSpecificity achieved 91.7% top-choice accuracy on 12 new substrates in experimental halogenase tests.
results.detail: Eight halogenases and 78 substrates were tested. The model was fine-tuned on a halogenase-specific dataset.
results.quote:
For the 12 
new substrates not previously seen in the database (Supplementary 
Fig. 49), the EZSpecificity-fine-tune model, which was fine-tuned using 
the HaloS dataset, achieved a prediction accuracy of 91.7% for its top 1  
recommendation (Fig. 5e).

results.finding: CATNIP tested 12 predicted substrates for TqaL; the second-ranked substrate yielded an oxidized product at 42% conversion.
results.detail: Four substrates were oxidized. Tests were conducted in triplicate; TqaL has a characterized homologue.

results.finding: Boltz-based classifiers beat both BLAST baselines on a CYP ranking benchmark of 45 held-out reactions.
results.detail: The holdout enzymes had under 40% sequence identity and substrates under 0.7 Tanimoto similarity to the remaining data. Each source organism had at least 10 candidate CYPs; retrieval was evaluated at the top 10%, 20% and 50%.
results.quote:
The consistent out-performance of both BLAST baselines is demonstrated
only by the output heads, trained in a supervised manner on CYP-specific data, and rivaling the most
performant enzyme-substrate model.

results.finding: CAFA5's head-to-head evaluation included 1,102 no-knowledge proteins; the top ten methods exceeded all baselines.
results.detail: The comparison covers the three GO aspects using information-weighted maximum F1. Some annotations in the full evaluation came from publications predating the submission deadline; the authors also examined a smaller, strictly unpublished subset.
results.quote: In all cases, the top-ten methods outperformed all baseline methods.

results.finding: In C. albicans, 245 of 2,746 screened genes were required for wrinkled colony biofilm formation.
results.detail: Mutants were scored on Spider agar after two days at 37°C; smooth or intermediate colonies were positive versus wrinkled wild type. GRACE strains received 100 µg/ml doxycycline. No tested predictor exceeded AUROC 0.60 for biofilm formation in either microbe. The phenotype does not establish molecular activity.
